module_title: Advent of Europeans - Policies, Settlements, and Decisive Battles
introduction: At this level, we will study the naval policies of Portuguese Governors, the trade 'farmans' (decrees) obtained by the English, and the decisive battles fought by the British against the Dutch and French to establish their trade monopoly.

core_concepts.title: Portuguese Policies (Almeida and Albuquerque)
core_concepts.description: Francisco de Almeida introduced the 'Blue Water Policy' to establish mastery over the Indian Ocean. Afonso de Albuquerque captured Goa from the Sultan of Bijapur in 1510 and encouraged his men to marry Indian women to build a local support base.

core_concepts.title: Early English Diplomacy
core_concepts.description: In 1615, Sir Thomas Roe arrived at Jahangir's court and successfully secured a farman to open factories across the Mughal Empire. In 1632, the Sultan of Golconda granted them the 'Golden Farman' for free trade in his ports.

core_concepts.title: Decline of the Dutch (Battle of Bedara - 1759)
core_concepts.description: The Dutch were primarily focused on the spice trade of Indonesia. Their Indian ambitions ended when the English decisively defeated them at the Battle of Bedara (Bengal) in 1759.

core_concepts.title: Battle of Wandiwash (1760)
core_concepts.description: The English and French fought the Carnatic Wars for supremacy in India. During the Third Carnatic War, the English forces led by Sir Eyre Coote decisively defeated the French under Count de Lally at Wandiwash in 1760.

core_concepts.title: Nature of the French Company
core_concepts.description: The French East India Company was formed in 1664 by Colbert, a minister of King Louis XIV. It was heavily controlled by the French government, which ultimately became a major reason for its failure.

important_entities.name: Afonso de Albuquerque
important_entities.significance: He captured Goa in 1510 and made early attempts to ban the practice of Sati in his territories.

important_entities.name: Joseph Francois Dupleix
important_entities.significance: He was the first to use the strategy of intervening in the internal disputes of Indian rulers to acquire territories and wealth (laying the groundwork for the 'Subsidiary Alliance').

important_entities.name: Sir Eyre Coote
important_entities.significance: He led the British forces to victory in the Battle of Wandiwash (1760), effectively ending the French threat to the British in India.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If options include both Masulipatnam (1611) and Surat (1613), remember: Masulipatnam was a 'temporary' settlement, while Surat was the first 'permanent' factory.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: First to come, Last to leave
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The Portuguese were the first Europeans to arrive in India (1498), but they were the last to leave. The Indian government had to launch 'Operation Vijay' in 1961 to liberate Goa from Portuguese rule.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Bedara beat the Dutch, Wandiwash washed away the French
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A simple way to remember which battle eliminated which rival European power.

exam_strategy_tips: Agricultural items brought by the Portuguese (tobacco, potato, tomato, cashew) and the printing press are highly tested facts.
Remember that both Captain Hawkins (1608) and Sir Thomas Roe (1615) visited the court of Mughal Emperor Jahangir.
